## Historical audit — S0133, chunk 2 of 3

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/generic_rsi/C2/test/commons_16007442/trajectory.jsonl`. All citations below refer to this file; offsets describe the supplied observations, not unseen chunks.

**Goal versus evidence.** The requested goal was a separate-mesh reconstruction of a single indoor photograph, matching viewpoint, framing, occlusions and materials. The student’s code interprets the scene as an electronics workbench. That interpretation and its landmark estimates are not independent verification of the photograph (line 13, `model_request`, characters [0,196930)).

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Initial scene and revision | The code constructs multiple named assemblies: bench, monitor, scope, meters, keyboard, lamp, cabinets, tools and clutter, with solid surfaces and individual parts. It specifies colors, screen emission and a proposed procedural desktop bump; actual texture appearance is unverified. A subsequent build resizes, rotates and moves the monitor display separately from its neck and foot, while retaining camera and light parameters. Grouping and intended support do not prove physical connection or contact (line 13, `model_request`, [0,196930)). |
| Feedback and adoption | The runner reports steps 1 and 2 successful with renders available and asks for a narrow, landmark-based comparison. The student’s next response explicitly diagnoses pale desktop and drawer fronts and changes those surface colors, retaining the camera and lighting. This demonstrates adoption of the **visible runner feedback procedure**, not receipt of a separate teacher’s diagnosis. No separate teacher input or teacher-driven update is visible in this chunk (lines 13 [0,196930), 15 `model_response` [0,15879)). |
| Exploration and validation | The student reports approximate reference/render landmarks and claims the monitor silhouette improved after step 2; these are student assessments, not independently checked images. The fresh third student session had no tool calls; the runner then executed its program (line 14 `codex_session` [0,3800); lines 15–16 [0,15879), [0,16518)). |
| Result | Step 3 reports `ok: true`, no error, a saved render and blend file; the trace selects step 3. Thus execution and selection succeeded, but visual or geometric correctness and any formal task score remain unknown. This is neither an empty patch nor an observed technical interruption or algorithm failure (lines 17 `execution_result` [0,74559), 18 `select` [0,58)). |

**Scene-specific uncertainty.** The program encodes a tilted meter, rotated keyboard and monitor, lamp arms, a camera and two area lights. It does not independently establish that pose, occlusions, object connections, framing, lighting or textures match the reference. The images themselves are not supplied to this audit. In particular, whether the monitor adjustment improved the match and whether darkening the desktop and cabinets corrected the alleged tone error remain hypotheses.

**Transferable lesson:** a render-backed, localized revision with explicit preserved regions makes intended changes traceable, but a successful render is not evidence of scene fidelity. **Task-specific lesson:** this student chose monitor geometry first and workbench/cabinet colors next; neither choice establishes a general best correction. Other chunks and any later assessment are outside the visible evidence.
